$comment: OBRA Level 2 dialogue. RULE: no line may name a drawable class -- checked word-boundary against all 50 ids AND display names. This level's vocabulary is unusually dangerous: the plaza is a SQUARE, the palms are TREES, the lit house has a DOOR, the offering is BREAD, the sky has a SUN and CLOUDS, and the birds are BIRDS. Every one of those is a class. They are phrased around: 'the plaza', 'the palms', 'the light in the window', 'something to eat', 'the light', 'the flock'. Tags appear in exactly one surface form, marked with **.

lines.text: Ay. She painted this one from the steps of the church, apo. Same hour, same heat. You can smell it.
The whole town is out. Do not let that fool you — the painting is in pieces, and the pieces did not walk off by themselves.
Two things before you start drawing. One: whatever you become, keep it under the strings. They are strung across the whole plaza and they will not move for you.
Two: nothing small. There are a hundred feet on this ground today and a float coming through later. They will not be looking down.
Hoy! I told you. Under the strings.
Naku. Come here. You are going to get yourself stepped on.
Not that one, apo. Too small for today. Pick something the crowd will see.
The church first. She never came to this one empty-handed — there was always a light to leave burning inside.
We have nothing to leave. So we get one. Look around, apo, the plaza is full of people who have what we need.
Three ways, and one of them is not drawing at all. Ask the dancers. They will want something back — they always do.
Or go round the houses. One of them has a light in the window, and something that can **unlock** will get you in.
Or clear them out of the way. Something that can **startle** — big enough that a crowd does not stay to argue.
So. How are we getting it?

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will dance for them.
Ha! Your lola danced that badly the first time too. They still gave her the flower.
Naku. You have your lola's feet. Go on — they are still waiting.
Never mind, apo. You have what we came for. Keep your feet — that is the important part.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: Someone is home. I will let myself in.
lines.text: Someone is home. I will let myself in.
We have done this before, you and I. You are faster now.
Take it and leave something on the sill. We are borrowing, not taking.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will clear the plaza.
Apo. If you do this they will not come back. Not today, not for us.
It is very quiet now. She painted this plaza full, apo. That is the only thing I wanted you to see.
Good. Inside, then. Wipe your feet.
Put it on the rack there. Not the middle — she always went to the left side, nearer the wall.
Do not look at me like that. A man can still have somewhere to put it.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: You are looking for her. She was here — this morning, in that pew, for a long while.

lines.speaker: priest
lines.text: When she left she went behind the plaza. There are two narrow ways back there, one after the other. It is dark in them even at this hour.
Two narrow ways. Of course. Come on, apo — before the light goes.
There. Look up. Five of them, and every one has a piece of her in its beak.
They are not stealing, apo. They are nesting. It is the same thing to us and not to them.
Three ways again. Bring them down gently — something that can **feed**. She did it every morning of her life.
Or put them up — something that can **startle**. They scatter, and they take her with them into the next one along.
Or knock them down. Something that can **strike** from where you stand. You will not get all five.
Quickly, apo. They are going higher.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will call them down.
Every morning, apo. Rain or no rain. She said they were the only ones who ever waited for her.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: Up you go, then.
Maybe they flew nearby. Come on — nothing is lost in a place this small.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.text: I will bring them down.
The rest got away. They will not have gone far — they never do.
Ah — here they are. Tangled in the strings, the whole line of them, flapping like the wash.
And two more pieces up there that were never in anybody's beak. The wind put those there.
Two ways only, apo, and I will not pretend otherwise. Go up to them — something that can **climb**, something you can set against the wall and stand on.
Do not try to go over. The strings are what you are reaching for, not something to get past.
Or bring the whole line down. Something that can **cut**. Faster. And the town wakes up tomorrow to bare poles.
Your hands, apo. Not mine.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I will go up to them.
lines.text: I will go up to them.
Slow, and everything still standing. She would have done it exactly that way and complained the whole time.

lines.speaker: apo
lines.choice_label: I will bring the line down.
lines.text: I will bring the line down.
They put those up at first light, apo. All of them, together. It took the morning.
Well. The way up is open now, at least. Nothing left to be in anyone's way.
Lay them out. Corners first — she taught me that and I never once did it.
There she is. Piyesta. Look how much of it is people, apo — she could not paint a plaza empty if she tried.
The fold runs right through it. That was us. That was a thing we did.
The next one is water, apo. She painted that one from a boat and she could not swim either. Come.
I cannot read it, apo. That is my eyes, not your hand — draw it bigger and slower.
There. Now I see it.
